label: lem:inf_conv
title: Lemma
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
et $(P,V)$ attain the minimum defining $K_{\mathrm{DK}}(R)$ and set $ a_{P,V} := \min \{ I(P,V), \, R \} $.
It can be readily verified that $|R - I(P,V)|^{+} = R - a_{P,V}$.
                 
                                    
                            
               
Since $I(P,V) \geq a_{P,V}$, the pair $(P,V)$ is feasible in the minimization defining $K_{\mathrm{O}}(a_{P,V})$, and $D(V \| W | P) \geq K_{\mathrm{O}}(a_{P,V})$.
It follows that
\begin{align*}
 K_{\mathrm{DK}}(R)   & = D(V \| W | P) + |R - I(P,V)|^{+} \\
    & \geq K_{\mathrm{O}}(a_{P,V}) + (R - a_{P,V}) \\
    & \geq \inf_{0 \leq a \leq R} \big\{ K_{\mathrm{O}}(a) + (R - a) \big\}.
\end{align*}
                                                                                   
                                                      
                  
                                                                                              
                

For the other direction, fix $a \in [0,R]$. If $K_{\mathrm{O}}(a) = +\infty$ there is nothing to prove. Otherwise, let $(P_a, V_a)$ attain the minimum defining $K_{\mathrm{O}}(a)$, so that $I(P_a,V_a) \geq a$ and $D(V_a \| W | P_a) = K_{\mathrm{O}}(a)$. Since $I(P_a,V_a) \geq a$ implies $|R - I(P_a,V_a)|^{+} \leq R - a$, we write
\begin{align*}
    K_{\mathrm{DK}}(R) & \leq D(V_a \| W | P_a) + |R - I(P_a,V_a)|^{+} \\
    & \leq K_{\mathrm{O}}(a) + (R - a),
\end{align*}
which holds for all $a \in [0,R]$. This completes the proof.

body_md: y Lemma~\ref{lem:inf_conv}, $K_{\mathrm{DK}}(R) = K_{\mathrm{O}}(R)$ holds if and only if the term $a = R$ attains the minimum in \eqref{eq:inf_conv}, that is, if and only if $K_{\mathrm{O}}(R) \leq K_{\mathrm{O}}(a) + (R - a)$ for all $a \in [0,R]$.

Since $\mathcal{M}$ is also non-empty and $I(P,V)$ is a continuous function of $P \times V$, the image of $\mathcal{M}$ under $I(\, \cdot \,,\, \cdot \,)$ is a closed interval, whose endpoints are $R_{\star}$ and $R^{\star}$ by \eqref{eq:R_star_def}. 

Finally, \eqref{eq:I_on_M} gives $I(P,V) \geq C_{\infty}(W)$ on $\mathcal{M}$, while $I(P,V) \leq \log|\mathcal{X}|$ and $I(P,V) \leq  H(Q^{\star})$ on $\mathcal{M}$.

label: cor:no_gap
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
here is no gap if and only if some $(P,V) \in \mathcal{M}$ has $I(P,V) = \log|\mathcal{X}|$. Since $I(P,V) \leq H(P) \leq \log|\mathcal{X}|$, this requires $P$ to be uniform and $I(P,V) = H(P)$, i.e., $X$ is a function of $Y$ under $P \times V$. 

Denoting this function by $\phi$, the support condition in the definition of $\mathcal{M}$ says that $W(y|\phi(y)) = \max_{x} W(y|x)$, and the condition $PV = Q^{\star}$ with $P$ uniform says that 
\begin{equation*}
  \sum_{y : \phi(y) = x} Q^{\star}(y) = \frac{1}{|\mathcal{X}|}, \ \text{for every } x,
\end{equation*}
which is \eqref{eq:equal_mass}. 
Conversely, given such a map $\phi$, the pair $(P,V)$ with $P(x)V(y|x) = Q^{\star}(y) \, \mathbbm{1}\{\phi(y) = x\}$ lies in $\mathcal{M}$, has uniform $P$, and satisfies $I(P,V) = \log|\mathcal{X}|$.

label: rem:gap_sufficient
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:gap_sufficient}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:interval}, a gap is present whenever $H(Q^{\star}) < \log|\mathcal{X}|$, since then we have $R^{\star} < \log|\mathcal{X}|$. This is the case whenever $|\mathcal{Y}| < |\mathcal{X}|$, and for every binary channel with $\max_{x} W(0|x) \neq \max_{x} W(1|x)$.
